title: Three consumed contracts and two platform reads of the petition have no dependency row, and two of the three operation names exist in no source
source: Template and Rules v1 sections R5.4 and R5.5 (DP-03, DP-07, DP-08, DP-13, DP-19); the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5021-APP (Depends on (build) RWB-S4-E5021-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; Contract, Integration and External dependencies None) and of RWB-S4-E5021-CON (all None); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T5.2, T6.1 and appendix T-A.1; Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 A2.21.2 and A2.21.3.3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (rwb-litigation: Partner issueInstruction, Decision child approval; IN NoticeDelivered and PartnerResultSubmitted) and slide 41; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-021 (Depends on FEAT-APD-01)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s10 Authority; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan; s18 Traceability; s19 Out of scope; CON s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s7 AC2 and AC6; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.8; s13
description: The two slices consume five things that no metadata row carries. (1) The D7.5 approval of rwb-decision, whose contract the plan names as RWB-P7-E2013-CON Approval routing with the delegation of authority table. (2) The rwb-case contract that reads the case route state and answers the route fact BANKRUPTCY_PETITION, because recovery_case and its route state are P3's and R-LIT-58 moves them. (3) The rwb-partner firm instruction, which Architecture v5 slide 19 names only as Partner: issueInstruction (law firm). (4) The reference-data read of LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, because DP-07 is not in either pattern set while TSD S4 T3.2 makes both lists required for action_type and status. (5) The Litigation right of each operation, because DP-08 is not in either pattern set and the rights of TSD S4 T6.1 have to be enforced somewhere. The approval contract is a P7 contract story, so it is a C dependency that does not block the build; the case and partner contracts are named in prose only, so their operation names are absent. The metadata keeps the plan's lists unchanged, both stories build on Day 1 against the fakes, and the five rows are recorded here.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), DP-07 (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), DP-08 (H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON) and DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the metadata rows of both slices carry Contract dependencies None; TSD S4 v2 T5.2 sends the case, the decision log, the access, the documents and the notices to their owners through published interfaces and names no operation; Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-litigation the partner instruction and the decision child with no path.
area: Contracts, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case, P7 rwb-decision and S9 rwb-partner
proposed: Keep both metadata rows as the plan gives them, name the five consumed rows in 12.2 and 12.8 of the app story and in 12.2 of the contract story, build against the fakes, and let step D1 decide whether RWB-P7-E2013-CON and a rwb-case contract story become C dependencies of this key.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-021, so both stories trace to the feature only
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-021 (metadata table: Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-21, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-APD-01, Decision; no requirement row); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-21; Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 Requirements served (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010, none naming a bankruptcy petition); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T8 (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 against FEAT-LIT-01 only)
section: Metadata row PRD reference of both stories; APP s2 Business rationale; s18 Traceability; the reqs key of both fragments; CON s2; s18
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-021 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-21 and the prerequisite FEAT-APD-01 and no requirement row, the plan's requirement list for both slices is empty, and the FSD S4 requirements table lists ten requirements of the module whose texts cover notices, the pack, the panel, court tracking, settlement, enforcement, deferral, prescription and proceeds but not the bankruptcy petition. The Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the feature one row and no requirement. Both stories therefore trace to FEAT-LIT-21 and to the L3 process 08 Litigate and enforce, and the requirement column carries the placeholder until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD of the module adds the identifiers. Nothing blocks the build; the exposure is a traceability report that cannot roll the stories up to a requirement.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-021 has seven rows and no requirement row; FSD S4 v3 Requirements served lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 with no petition requirement; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row FEAT-LIT-21 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind User, Primary role Enforcement owner, Systems LIT and Partner portal, Depends on FEAT-APD-01 and no requirement; TSD S4 v2 T8 maps its ten requirements to FEAT-LIT-01 with the story column reading Written one epic ahead.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the business analyst
proposed: Trace both stories to FEAT-LIT-21 and process 08 Litigate and enforce, write no identifier by pattern, and let the Epics 3 to 8 PRD and step D1 add the requirement and update the reqs list of both fragments.

title: The catalogue lists LawsuitFiled on the litigation topic but assigns no story to it, so the filing of a bankruptcy petition is tied to no event
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (rwb-litigation OUT: event topic rwb.litigation.events.v1 carrying LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult) and slide 43 (JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult with producers and consumers; LawsuitFiled with no consumer row); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 and the pattern set of this key (DP03, DP13, DP19); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T5.3 (Events: None)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s12.3 Events published; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.6 Schedules; s17 Guardrails; CON s7 AC8; s12.3; s12.4; the events_published key of both fragments
description: LawsuitFiled is published on rwb.litigation.events.v1 by the event catalogue and the catalogue row gives it no consumer and no producer story. The petition is the case type a court filing produces, so a reader may reasonably expect the filing of a petition to raise LawsuitFiled; but DP-09 is not in either pattern set, no outbox row or producer is added by the two stories, and no source states that the petition filing is that event's trigger. Declaring it would put an event into the build that no owner assigned, and omitting it silently would leave an event of the service with no story. Both slices therefore publish nothing, the decision record reaches the shared topic only through the local decision-record library of DP-03, and the assignment is recorded here.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult; slide 43 gives JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult their consumers and gives LawsuitFiled no consumer row; TSD S4 v2 T5.3 declares the event direction as None; the patterns of both slices are DP03, DP13 and DP19 and none is DP-09.
area: Event contract, S4 rwb-litigation with S5 rwb-asset and P3 rwb-case
proposed: Publish no event from either slice, keep the catalogue unchanged, and let the event catalogue owner assign LawsuitFiled to a story; a later assignment adds one outbox row, one DP-09 pattern and one criterion to that story and no change to the legal_action row shape.

title: The D7.5 approval child workflow has no type name, workflow ID or queue registration beyond the queue of rwb-decision
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (rwb-litigation TMP: Decision child approval) and slide 14 (rwb-decision TMP: child approval); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13, 27 and 28 (approval from the workflow kit, DoA lookup as a parameter, each stage a child on the owner's queue, durable timers and retry policy); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 (service level 5 working days, owner Approver at D7.5)
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 8; s12.5 Workflows and activities; s12.6 Schedules; s13 Solution plan; CON s11 Data; s12.5
description: R-LIT-58 gives the petition a 5-working-day answer time and Architecture v5 gives rwb-litigation a child workflow named Decision child approval, but no source names that child's workflow type, its workflow ID convention, its queue registration beyond on rwb-decision, what happens to the petition when the service level expires, or whether the clock is the child's durable timer or a timer of this service. The Temporal design names ApprovalWorkflow as the kit template on rwb-decision for the route decision of S1 and describes the generic approval template as maker-checker with the DoA lookup as a parameter; it never states that the D7.5 petition approval uses the same type. The two stories therefore declare the clock as the approval workflow's and not their own, name no child type, and carry the mapping here.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 TMP Partner issueInstruction (law firm), Comms child demand notice, Decision child approval; Temporal design slide 12 note Approval (maker-checker, DoA lookup as a parameter); slide 13 note each stage is a child workflow started on the owner's queue; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 service level 5 working days with owner Approver at D7.5.
area: Workflow, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision
proposed: Carry the 5 working days as the approval child's durable timer on queue rwb-decision, name the child by the decision point D7.5 and the queue only, and let the Temporal catalogue fix its type name and workflow ID.

title: The approval contract publishes no operation that raises an approval item, so the petition's take-to-the-approver shape has no owner
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P7 rwb-decision (Decision and rules)/RWB P7 E2013 CON Approval routing with the delegation of authority table - contract v1.md section 12.1 and its gap CG-B-P7-01-E2013-5; Recovery Workbench TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.1 (approval reads and the three decisions only); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-021 AC1 and AC2; Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 appendix T-A.1
section: APP s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow step 7; s10 Authority; s12.2; s19 Out of scope; CON s2; s3; s7 AC2 and AC5; s11 Data; s12.2
description: Both stories have to take the petition to the approver at D7.5, and the only approval document of the target is RWB-P7-E2013-CON, which publishes the approval reads and the three decisions and no operation that creates an approval item; that document says so itself and carries the absence as its own gap. The result for this key is that the request shape of the petition's approval is fixed nowhere: the case reference, the decision code, the capability area, the product group, the amount, the source type and reference, the rule and its version and the Idempotency-Key are the elements the approval table of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 gives, and the object that carries them to rwb-decision has no published operation, no field set and no error set. Both stories build against the P7 fake and carry the placeholder rather than invent a path.
evidence: RWB-P7-E2013-CON section 12.1 publishes the approval reads and the approve, return and refuse operations and states that no operation creates an approval, carrying CG-B-P7-01-E2013-5; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 lists the same operations and no raise; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 lists five S4 operations and no approval operation; legacy AC1 and AC2 say takes the petition to the approver and route the petition to the approver at D7.5.
area: Contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect with the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: Build the approval call against the P7 fake with the approval-row elements of the data dictionary, keep the placeholder on the operation name, and have rwb-decision publish the raise operation and its field set; when it publishes, the call and the fake change and no row of this service does.

title: Five values of the petition exist in no source: the bankruptcy test, the approver role at D7.5, the index set of legal_action, the status of a refused petition and the 400 answer
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 (condition enforcement exhausted and the bankruptcy test is met; owner Approver at D7.5); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 T3.1 (legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and no index row), T3.2 (LOV-LEGAL-STATUS with six values and no refusal value), T6.1 (roles RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-LEGAL, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-HEADLIT and others, none named as the D7.5 approver), T-A.2 (errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 and no 400); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 A2.21.3.1 (VR-S4-021-1, R-LIT-58, BR-S4-021 only)
section: APP s5 Exception paths; s8 Business rules; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.1; s13 Solution plan; s14 Validation and messages; s15 Screens and states; CON s7 AC3 and AC4; s9; s11; s12.1; s13; s14
description: Five values that both stories need are given by no source read for this key. (1) The bankruptcy test: R-LIT-58's condition names it and no source defines it, so its rows and threshold are unknown. (2) The approver role at D7.5: the rule names Approver at D7.5 as the owner and the TSD S4 T6.1 matrix names no role as that approver, so the route code the approval needs is unknown. (3) The index set of legal_action: the TSD gives the columns and the primary key and lists no index, while the workspace read needs a lookup by case_id. (4) The status of a petition refused before filing: LOV-LEGAL-STATUS has six values and none names a refusal, and R-LIT-60 moves the case, not the legal action. (5) The 400 answer: the three S4 T-A.2 rows name 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and no source names a 400 for a body the service cannot parse. Each is written as the placeholder with this pair rather than guessed.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-58 condition column enforcement exhausted and the bankruptcy test is met and owner column Approver at D7.5; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 has no index or key row for legal_action; T3.2 LOV-LEGAL-STATUS OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN; T6.1 has no D7.5 approver row; T-A.2 error sets carry no 400; FSD S4 v3 A2.21.3.1 lists VR-S4-021-1, R-LIT-58 and BR-S4-021 only.
area: Rules, data and error set, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the data steward
proposed: Carry the bankruptcy test and the filing window as versioned reference rule rows, read the D7.5 approver role as a route parameter of the approval, declare only the primary key on id in the DDL template, keep a refused petition at status OPEN with the refusal on the decision record, and answer 400 with the platform problem document; settle each value with its owner and add no code constant.

title: The FSD S4 and the TSD S4 that the two slices read are In review with an empty sign-off table and the realigned stories have no approval
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (document control, document sign-off); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (document control, document sign-off); Template and Rules v1 R8.1; AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10
section: Metadata row Status of both stories; APP s3 Preconditions; CON s3 Preconditions
description: The sources of both slices are not approved. The FSD S4 is at version 3 in review with an empty sign-off table and the TSD S4 is at version 2 in review with an empty sign-off table, and the run of D-RCV-60 has no human approval step, so the missing approval is recorded as an assumption, both stories carry Status Draft (realignment v1) and the work continues. No behaviour and no value of either story depends on a signature, and no status of a source document is changed.
evidence: FSD S4 document control gives Status In review and its document sign-off table has empty role, name, signature and date cells; TSD S4 v2 document control gives Status In review and its sign-off table is empty; Template and Rules v1 R8.1 asks every new document for a change-log row naming D-RCV-60 and the tool line; AGENTS.md rule 9 says a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the work continues in Draft.
owner_role: Solution architect and the business owner of S4
proposed: Keep both stories at Draft (realignment v1) and let the verification loop collect the sign-offs before any status changes.
